summary: Concretised 'conductor' for the (★) word set S = {4uBC−u−B : u,B,C ≥ 1} (any u,B; the identity 4/n = 1/(uBC)+1/(nBC)+1/(nuC) needs no coprimality) and computed its gap set exactly for all odd n ≤ 10⁹ (C sieve, 3 min) plus the non-square gaps in (10⁹, 4·10⁹]. Gaps ≤ 10⁹: all 15 810 odd squares (T1, PROVED) and 1 154 non-squares (458 ≡ 1, 696 ≡ 3 mod 4; 24 primes, among them exactly the 14 (★)-failing p ≡ 1 (4) of FRONTIER §2.1, last 8 813 281); non-square gaps per decade 2, 7, 20, 68, 145, 239, 299, 229, 145 for 10⁰…10⁸, then 63 in (10⁹, 4·10⁹] (no primes, 61 divisible by 3), largest 3 998 270 265 = 3·5·11·89·272269 — still near the top of the range, so no conductor is visible (EVIDENCE). No single level or finite set of levels has a conductor: the share of odd non-squares ≤ 10⁹ with no word at C ≤ K is 27.8 %, 4.7 %, 0.50 %, 0.068 %, 0.0041 % for K = 1, 4, 16, 64, 1024, and every finite set of pairs (u,B) misses every n ≡ 1 mod lcm(4uB) (would need 4uB | u+B+1, impossible; PROVED), so the semigroup notion only fits each single AP n ≡ −(u+B) (mod 4uB), which has conductor 4uB−u−B trivially. S is not additively closed (S+S has no odd elements) and words with t = 4C are not Frobenius numbers of ⟨a,b⟩ ((4Cu−1)(4Cv−1) = 4Cn+1, so g(a,b) = 4Cn+1−a−b ≠ n); only t = 1 is Sylvester's case (Pass 1).
not_done: No proof or heuristic fit of the falling decade counts. Not run beyond 4·10⁹ (no levels recorded above 10⁹). The coprime-pair count R* (more zeros, see BOARD2_SLATE.md:177) not recomputed. The alt step (an exact ansatz with an additive free coordinate) is covered by the AP remark only.
next: If wanted, fit the per-decade non-square gap counts against exp(−c·M_BM(n)) to test whether the non-square gap set is finite.

summary: Substitution (stated): instead of an F₂ carry circuit I used the natural integer encoding — binary digits of u,B,C ∈ [1,2^k] (n = 3k Boolean variables), the single equation P = 4uBC−u−B−p and x_i² = x_i over ℚ (computed mod two primes ≈ 2³¹) — for which the minimal Nullstellensatz degree is exactly deg ML(1/P) + 3, ML = multilinear interpolant on the cube (PROVED in the script docstring). For k = 4…7 (12–21 variables) I computed it on (★)-failing primes 409, 577, 5569, 9601 (and 2521), on odd squares 441, 625, 2025, 9801 (T1, infeasible at every height) and on 12 control primes with R(p) > 0 but an empty box: in every instance the degree is maximal (= n, so NS degree n+3), all 2ⁿ coefficients are non-zero and the two moduli agree. The one-hot encoding refutes every infeasible instance in degree 3 (Σ x_u y_B z_C = 1), so it is equally uninformative. The bounded refutation degree does not tell structural (T1), sporadic (409) and box-only infeasibility apart (EVIDENCE).
not_done: F₂ circuit encodings (carry variables; degree needs F₂ linear algebra over huge monomial spaces) not computed. Positivstellensatz/SOS degree not computed. The ES₅/I3_𝒞 systems at p = 5, 13, 17 named in the item were not encoded; only the (★) system was.
next: None; the measure is encoding-generic in both natural encodings tried.

summary: Literature step done: a web search, plus reading Schwartz, 'Application of Egyptian Fractions to Parallel Resistors' (ASEE Mid-Atlantic 2018, PDF), which treats only two integer resistors in parallel through the classical parametrisation (R₁−R)(R₂−R) = R² with (τ(R²)−1)/2 realisations — exactly ES's second step 4/n − 1/x = 1/y + 1/z. The resistor-network literature found (Khan arXiv:1004.3346; Khan, Resonance 2012; Amengual, Am. J. Phys. 68 (2000) 175; Eppstein's 'Egyptian fractions & parallel resistors' page) counts or bounds the series–parallel resistances of n unit resistors and gives pedagogy, with no realisability result for k parallel branches that are single integer resistors. In the general network setting every positive rational is realisable (Euclid/continued fractions), so the restriction to three single-resistor branches is ES itself, with no network-theoretic handle.
not_done: Amengual 2000 and Khan 2012 read at abstract level only. The squared-rectangle/Kirchhoff (Brooks–Smith–Stone–Tutte) angle not pursued.

summary: Made concrete: Lehmer's condition in Egyptian form is Π(1−1/p_i) = (1−1/n)/k for squarefree n = p₁…p_r with kφ(n) = n−1, and its exclusion tools are linear-local (q | n and q | φ(n) is contradictory, which forces n squarefree; 3 | n rules out every p ≡ 1 (3)) and archimedean (Π p/(p−1) > k, giving ω(n) ≥ 14 (Cohen–Hagis) and n < r^{2^r} (Pomerance 1977)). Tested on the repo's constrained-ES failure sets: archimedean bounds explain none, and T1 (odd squares) is a quadratic-character/BM argument, not a linear-local one; the only Lehmer-type linear-local effect in (★) is the lemma 'q | n and q | u ⇒ q | B' (PROVED from n ≡ −(u+B) mod 4uB). It is visible in the Z1018 data — of the 912 non-square (★)-gaps in (10⁵, 10⁹], 88.7 % are divisible by 3 (baseline 33.3 %), 44.5 % by 5 (20 %) and 36 % by 7 (14.3 %) (EVIDENCE) — but it only thins the admissible pairs (pairs with q ∤ uB stay), so it explains density, never exclusion. A web search found no Lehmer→Egyptian-fraction method transfer (the known Egyptian siblings are the Giuga/Znám equations).
evidence: web search 'Lehmer totient problem Egyptian fraction' (2026-11-01)
not_done: Cohen–Hagis and Pomerance papers not read in full (statements from standard references). No test of whether the 3-divisibility enrichment is fully explained by the lemma (e.g. by comparing pair-count densities).

summary: Premise check: ES(n) is Δ₀ (bounded search x ≤ 3n/4, y ≤ 2nx/(4x−n); BL Lemma 3.10), so the good set and the failure set are both recursive — the good set is Diophantine directly, with no MRDP needed, and the failure set is Diophantine by MRDP — and ES is equivalent to one specific polynomial having no positive value, the generic Π₁ fact. I made the 'polynomial certificate world' explicit: P = (1+Σd_i²)(1−D²), with D = 4xyz − n(xy+yz+zx) and n, x, y, z each 1 + a sum of four squares, has 16 variables, total degree 14 and 64 124 monomials. A brute-force check confirms its positive values in 2…150 are exactly the ES-good n (here all of them). P > 0 ⟺ D = 0, so P carries exactly one solution's information: a tautological certificate with no arithmetic content.
not_done: No explicit (Jones/MRDP-style) polynomial for the failure set was built (huge and uninformative). No logician contacted.

summary: Read McMullen's 'Uniformly Diophantine numbers in a fixed real quadratic field' (author PDF) §§1–3: the construction L_m = U^m + U^{−m}A (Thm 2.2) has |det L_m| = f_{2m}, a generalised Fibonacci number, and is fixed by U^{2m} because U^m ≡ ±f_{m+1}I (mod f_m) (Prop 2.1, eq. 2.6), so the trick prescribes the field but a determinant only along the exponentially sparse f_{2m} (a Lucas-sequence identity, like the repo's thin families), never an arbitrary p. Direct transfer test: a (★) certificate is M = [[d₁,p],[4C,d₂]] ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with t² − 4 = 16C(Cw²+p), w = (d₁−d₂)/4C (PROVED), so its trace field Q(√(C(Cw²+p))) moves with p. For each fixed K = Q(√D₀) (121 squarefree D₀ < 200) I counted primes p ≡ 1 (4) with a certificate whose trace field is K: the union over all 121 fields is 236/39 175 (p ≤ 10⁶), 809/332 180 (10⁷) and 2 464/≈2.88·10⁶ (10⁸) primes, growing like X^{1/2} as predicted (traces in K are geometric and t ≥ 4√p); the best field, D₀ = 30, has 102 primes ≤ 10⁷ and 90 of the 121 fields have none. So 'ES in a fixed quadratic field' fails for almost all p (EVIDENCE + the √X heuristic).
not_done: McMullen §§4–6 (CF patterns, heights) skimmed only. The loop-generator/Hecke variant (§3) not tested for prescribing an off-diagonal entry. No bounded-partial-quotient filter applied to the certificates.
next: None; McMullen-type uniformity needs an exponential conductor sequence, while ES needs every p.

summary: Did the phrasing step (identities checked with sympy): with m = 4x−n and N = nx the second step is m/N = 1/y + 1/z ⟺ (my−N)(mz−N) = N², an exact value of the split product form XY on the coset (−N,−N) + mℤ² — a rank-one diagonal (A ⊂ SL₂) problem whose A-orbit is divergent (the form is split over ℚ) and which asks for equality, not smallness, so the count is a divisor function (ET's parametrisation). The full equation is not a norm form either: with X = 4x−n etc., XYZ − n²(X+Y+Z+2n) = 16·(4xyz − n(xy+yz+zx)), a product of three linear forms plus a linear term, not invariant under any diagonal action. EKL needs a rank-≥2 diagonal action with positive entropy and gives dimension/almost-every statements, so no diagonal-action reading of ES exists to which measure rigidity applies.
evidence: sympy identity check (both identities expand to 0; run inline, recorded here)
not_done: EKL paper not reread. No test of approximate (inequality) relaxations of ES, e.g. inf over x of ‖·‖-products.

summary: Inspected the finite reductions: Tao (arXiv:1701.02048) shows integer speeds of size n^{O(n²)} suffice, and Malikiosis–Santos–Schymura (arXiv:2411.06903) improve this to binom(n+1,2)^{n−1} via LR zonotopes (abstracts read); both rest on an n-dimensional speed parameter with an open (robust) witness condition ‖tv_i‖ ≥ 1/(n+1), so large speeds can be approximated by smaller ones and the witness time transfers. ES's witness is exact divisibility, and a (★) witness (u,B) transfers only along its progression n ≡ −(u+B) (mod 4uB), so a 'finite checking' statement for ES would be a finite covering by such progressions. That is impossible (PROVED, elementary): for any finite set of pairs with L = lcm(4uB), primes p ≡ 1 (mod L) — infinitely many by Dirichlet — would need 4uB | u+B+1, which fails since 4uB > u+B+1 ≥ 1. The numbers in Z1018 show this concretely: words at levels C ≤ K leave 4.7 %, 0.50 % and 0.0041 % of odd non-squares ≤ 10⁹ uncovered for K = 4, 16, 1024.
not_done: Neither paper read beyond the abstract. No ES analogue of the zonotope/covering-radius reformulation attempted.

summary: Read Graham, Pacific J. Math. 14 (1964) 85–92 (msp.org PDF): Theorem 4 says p/q is a finite sum of reciprocals of distinct nth powers iff p/q ∈ ∪_{π∈P}[π, π + ζ(n) − Σ_{j≤t_n} j^{−n}) with t_n ~ n/ln 2, t₂ = 1; for squares this is p/q ∈ [0, π²/6−1) ∪ [1, π²/6) — purely archimedean, with no denominator condition — so the item's premise ('finite exception list') is false: the exceptions are all rationals in the gaps, infinitely many (local conditions appear only in the variants Cor. A, distinct odd squares iff q is odd and p/q ∈ [0, π²/8−1) ∪ [1, π²/8), and Cor. B, squares ≡ 4 (mod 5) needing (q,5) = 1). The method is the expected thick reservoir: Theorem A (Graham's earlier completeness theorem + every large integer is a sum of distinct nth powers) reduces representability to approximability from above with unboundedly many terms ('smoothly replaceable' tails), and the remarks concede explicit term bounds are astronomically large. Corollary for the ES family (PROVED from Cor. 1): 4/n is a finite sum of distinct reciprocal squares iff n ∉ {1,2,5,6} — an archimedean finite exception list, the opposite of ES's fixed-length, arithmetic difficulty. The printed examples 1/2 and 1/3 were checked exactly.
not_done: Graham's companion paper [2] (completeness theorem) not read.

summary: The outreach itself (emailing Bright–Loughran) is not done, but its mathematical question — does a finer invariant (finite descent, étale–Brauer, Harpaz/Harpaz–Wittenberg integral-point methods) apply to U_n — is answered in BRAINSTORM/z45_etale_descent.md §0 and Props 1–5: 'π₁(U_n)=1, π₁(Ũ_n)=1, but π₁(U_n^sm)=ℤ/2 … ordinary finite descent and étale–Brauer on the singular surface or its resolution add nothing to BL. Even on the smooth locus, finite descent and its entire ordinary Brauer group simultaneously leave positive integral adeles for every n≥2.' The same file checks Harpaz–Schlank Thm 11.1 and Harpaz JEMS 2019 Thm 1.0.1 (no isomorphism of the ES target to his pencils), and BRAINSTORM/s9_fibration_level.md covers the fibration method. I re-read BL (arXiv:1908.02526): ES is strong approximation for W = U_n(ℝ)₊ × Π U_n(ℤ_p), and Thm 1.9 (BM is not the only obstruction to strong approximation, for every n) comes from real/finiteness considerations (Lemmas 3.10–3.11), not from a finer adelic invariant. The one open point an email could ask about is z45's stated uncomputed set ⋃_d q_d((Y_d∖0)(𝔸)^{Br(Y_d)}) ∩ W^sm.

summary: Wrote ES in ⟨ℕ,+,|⟩ without multiplication (PROVED, elementary; brute-force checked for all odd n < 20 001 and all 428 primes < 3 001): (★)(n) ⟺ ∃u,m ≥ 1: 4u | m+1 ∧ m | n+u, and TypeII(p) ⟺ ∃e,N,a,b,y: p+e = 4N ∧ a|N ∧ b|N ∧ b|y ∧ a|y+1 ∧ e|a+b, so 'every prime p ≡ 1 (4) has a Type II solution' is a ∀∃ sentence of Presburger arithmetic plus divisibility. Against the known decidable fragments: for fixed p, ES(p) is a bounded ∃-sentence (Lipshitz/Bel'tyukov, trivially), while Bozga–Iosif (FoSSaCS 2005, read) prove L^(n)_| decidable and the positive ∃L^(n)_| fragment decidable only when every variable left of | is quantified outermost, and cite the ∃∀ fragment as undecidable; ES's divisor variables depend on the universal p, so the sentence lies in the undecidable ∀∃ class, and moving the divisors outermost means fixing the moduli, i.e. a finite congruence covering (B1). A Lipshitz-type local–global principle also fails at p = 409: the (★) system is ℓ-adically solvable at every ℓ (u = 1, m = 3, or m = 7 at ℓ = 3) and meets the order constraints, yet has no solution. The reason is that the divisibilities force bounded, non-spaced variables (3u ≤ p+1).
not_done: Lipshitz 1978 not read (decidability statement taken from Bozga–Iosif's citation). Type I not linearised (it needs the product pe). No formal undecidability proof for this particular sentence class.

summary: Built the grid and checked it: rows are levels C, vertices the sorted divisors d of 4Cp+1 at x = log d/log N, labels A (d ≡ 1), B (d ≡ −1, a certificate) and O (other) mod 4C, and consecutive rows are joined by a sweep triangulation. Boundary facts (PROVED): both side columns are always A, and d ↦ N/d maps class c to c⁻¹, preserving the labels, so every row is a palindrome whose middle edge (if any) is monochromatic and has an even number of edges of each label pair; the Sperner boundary degree is therefore always even and Sperner/Tucker never force a fully labelled cell (Tucker is vacuous anyway, because the self-inverse classes ±1, including d = 1, would need label 0). Check for all 1 125 primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 20 000 with 40 levels: 0 non-palindromic rows, 0 odd boundary parities, an even number of fully labelled triangles in every grid, and never one without a certificate (1 092 grids have such triangles; 1 120 have certificates).
not_done: The alt labelling of lattice points (x,y) ∈ [p/4,p]² by the sign/residue of 4xy − p(x+y) was not built. Only one triangulation scheme was used (the parity statement does not depend on it).
